methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $380M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ZeroAvia is a Series C-stage transportation company that has raised $380M+ to date. The comparable universe in Transportation includes 8 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, Harbinger, and others) and no direct public comparables. The narrow peer set at ZeroAvia's stage and valuation tier limits reliance on public market multiples.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($380M) as a proxy for post-Series B valuation and applying a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier to Series C produces an implied valuation of $646M. This reflects observed progression patterns across venture stages where capital influx and market validation drive valuations upward between funding rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $549M to $743M, centered on $646M. The range reflects ±15% variance around the median to account for execution risk and market timing. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage Transportation peers with sufficient trading or funding data to apply triangulated multiples, and ZeroAvia's early-stage commercialization relative to larger-cap competitors like Rivian. The stage-progression method is the sole applicable approach here; broader sectoral comparables would introduce material bias given ZeroAvia's specialized hydrogen-electric propulsion focus within a heterogeneous Transportation sector.
